title: Robots can handle a third of physical jobs — but not yet cost-effectively: Anthropic
key_facts: An Anthropic analysis says about 300,000 US jobs are exposed to robots that are cost-effective today.
If robot costs fell 20%, that could rise to 2.8 million jobs; based on historical declines of about 3% a year, that could take seven years.
Robots in structured settings such as assembly lines can do almost 50% of physical tasks; in unstructured settings such as construction sites, under 2%; in warehouses, about 22%.
Taxi drivers have the highest exposure, 2.2 on a 0-3 scale.
A robot doing the work of 14 packers would cost less than the workers over a 10-year life, per the analysis ($2 million purchase and $45,000 yearly running costs versus a typical $49,000 salary).
Jobs needing dexterity in unstructured settings or interpersonal skill are least at risk.
quote_evidence: Taxi drivers have an exposure rate of 2.2, the highest of all work, on a 0-3 index scale.
Few of the jobs outside of environments specifically structured for robots are cost-competitive today, but that could change as costs for the technology and hardware come down.
If costs dropped 20%, then the 300,000 jobs that are cost-competitive today would increase to 2.8 million.
why_it_matters_hint: Robots can already do a third of physical tasks, but cost keeps most jobs safe for now.
notes: Report publication date not stated; Facilities Dive summary of the Anthropic analysis only. 'A third' is from the headline.
